correctness.rationale: For the zero-mean Kirchhoff Laplacian L=-d^2/ds^2 on a connected finite compact loopless metric multigraph, f(x)=<Lf,g(x,.)> and Cauchy–Schwarz give the exact point-evaluation norm Q(x)=||g(x,.)||_2^2 and equality only along L^{-1}g. Vertex Green functions solve a finite weighted Laplacian with source 1_a-(sum incident lengths)/(2T), and the normalization of edge-integrated quadratic polynomials fixes the additive constant. For an interior point x_t of edge (a,b), the global Green kernel equals (1-t)g_a+t g_b plus a same-edge Dirichlet tent of height ell and minus its mean ell^2t(1-t)/(2T). Expanding its square gives an exact degree<=4 polynomial for every t, not sampled interpolation. Endpoint/cubic stationary roots/flat edges exhaust the extrema. The t^4 coefficient ell^2(ell-r_ab-ell^2/T)/3 follows from the Green-potential resistance identity; Foster trace gives sum 3p_e/ell_e^3=beta_1-1. Bridges give negative leading coefficient, and beta_1>=2 forces some positive one. Independent Neumann spectral zeta checks reproduce Q(0)=T^3/45 and Q(T/2)=T^3/720 for T=1, verifying interval boundary normalization. The inspected checker independently subdivides edges into new Kirchhoff vertices and compares exact rational kernels for finitely many multigraphs; that is corroborative, not a general proof.

evidence: The published universal first-order sharp Sobolev evaluation formula has quadratic edge profiles and an analogous beta_1-1 curvature identity.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Different energy: ||f′||² leads to Green diagonal g(x,x), whereas ||f′′||² on the Kirchhoff domain leads to ||g(x,.)||² and quartic edge envelopes. The first-order theorem cannot be substituted to obtain this sharp H² constant.
